components.note: 言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters: a warning is spoken.
敬 (jìng, respect) is a close sound clue for jǐng.
宀 (roof) — a public building where officials work; 官 is an official.
官 (guān) gives the sound of 管 guǎn, 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.pinyin: Jǐngguān, qǐng bāngbang wǒ.
example.english: Officer, please help me.
example.fact: 警官 typically works as a title used to address or refer to an individual police officer by rank, while 警察 is the broader, more common word for "police" as an occupation or institution — roughly the same split as English "officer" versus "police."

examples.hanzi: 警官让我们在这里等一下。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngguān ràng wǒmen zài zhèlǐ děng yíxià.
examples.english: The police officer asked us to wait here for a moment.

examples.hanzi: 那位警官每天在路口指挥交通。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi jǐngguān měi tiān zài lùkǒu zhǐhuī jiāotōng.
examples.english: That police officer directs traffic at the crossing every day.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.

example.hanzi: 她今天穿的裙子很性感。
example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān chuān de qúnzi hěn xìnggǎn.
example.english: The dress she's wearing today is very sexy.
example.fact: 性感 combines 性 ("sex, nature") with 感 ("feeling, sense") — literally "a sexual feeling" — an almost exact structural parallel to how English "sexy" grew out of the noun "sex" plus the adjective-forming "-y."

examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē hěn xìnggǎn.
examples.english: This song is very sexy.

examples.hanzi: 她觉得自信的人最性感。
examples.pinyin: Tā juéde zìxìn de rén zuì xìnggǎn.
examples.english: She thinks confident people are the most attractive.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).

example.hanzi: 他因为压力太大而选择了自杀。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi yālì tài dà ér xuǎnzéle zìshā.
example.english: He chose to end his own life because the pressure became too much.
example.fact: 自杀 is a reflexive verb-object compound, literally "self-kill" (自 "self" + 杀 "to kill") — the same reflexive 自- element that opens 自己 ("oneself") and 自我 ("self, ego"), all marking that an action's target is the subject itself.

examples.hanzi: 遇到困难时，要及时向别人求助，不要想到自杀。
examples.pinyin: Yùdào kùnnán shí, yào jíshí xiàng biéren qiúzhù, búyào xiǎngdào zìshā.
examples.english: When you run into trouble, ask others for help in time and don't think of suicide.

examples.hanzi: 新闻报道要谨慎处理自杀的话题。
examples.pinyin: Xīnwén bàodào yào jǐnshèn chǔlǐ zìshā de huàtí.
examples.english: News reports should handle the topic of suicide with care.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks and flavors: 醉 drunk, 醒 sober, 酸 sour, 配 match; 酒 is liquor, with 氵 for the liquid.
酉 also hints at the sound: yǒu is close to jiǔ.
口 (mouth) — speech sounds and particles: 吗, 呢, 啊; 吧 is a suggestion particle, or the bar in 酒吧.
巴 (bā) sounds exactly like 吧; also in 爸 bà, 把 bǎ, 爬 pá.

example.hanzi: 我们晚上去酒吧喝一杯吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshang qù jiǔbā hē yì bēi ba.
example.english: Let's go to a bar for a drink tonight.
example.fact: 吧 in 酒吧 is a phonetic loan borrowed purely for its sound to render English "bar," not for any meaning of its own — the same borrowed 吧 shows up in 迪吧 (dībā, "disco") and 网吧 (wǎngbā, "internet café"), a small family of "X-bar" loanwords.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔbā wǎnshang yǒu yīnyuè.
examples.english: This bar has music in the evening.

examples.hanzi: 他在酒吧里认识了很多朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiǔbā lǐ rènshile hěn duō péngyou.
examples.english: He met many friends at the bar.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to ask or discuss.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.

example.hanzi: 我们下午要讨论这个计划。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xiàwǔ yào tǎolùn zhège jìhuà.
example.english: We're going to discuss this plan in the afternoon.
example.fact: 讨论 takes its object directly with no preposition needed (讨论这个问题, "discuss this problem") — a common trap for English speakers who reflexively want to add "about" after "discuss," a habit that doesn't carry over into Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 我们来讨论一下这个问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen lái tǎolùn yíxià zhè ge wèntí.
examples.english: Let's discuss this problem.

examples.pinyin: Dàjiā tǎolùn de hěn rèliè.
examples.english: Everyone discussed it enthusiastically.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen liǎ yǒu tóngyàng de àihào.
example.english: The two of us have the same hobbies.
example.fact: 同样 usually sits directly before a noun as an attributive ("the same X") or before a clause meaning "likewise," while its near-synonym 一样 (also in this deck) more often follows a comparison frame like "A 跟 B 一样" — both mean "same" but favor different positions in the sentence.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen tóngyàng xǐhuan tīng yīnyuè.
examples.english: We both like listening to music equally.

examples.hanzi: 同样的错误不要犯两次。
examples.pinyin: Tóngyàng de cuòwù búyào fàn liǎng cì.
examples.english: Don't make the same mistake twice.

components.note: 身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 份 is a person's portion or share.
分 (fēn) is a near sound match for fèn; also 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.

example.pinyin: Qǐng chūshì nín de shēnfènzhèng.
example.english: Please show your ID card.
example.fact: 身份 shows up constantly in the compound 身份证 (shēnfènzhèng, literally "identity-proof-certificate") — one of the most important pieces of paperwork in daily life in China, required for everything from buying train tickets to checking into a hotel.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng yǐncáng zìjǐ de shēnfèn.
examples.english: He wants to hide his identity.

examples.hanzi: 作为学生，你的身份是什么？
examples.pinyin: Zuòwéi xuésheng, nǐ de shēnfèn shì shénme?
examples.english: As a student, what is your role?

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.
日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.

example.hanzi: 请你说明一下这个规则。
example.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ shuōmíng yíxià zhège guīzé.
example.english: Please explain this rule.
example.fact: 说明 works as both a verb ("to explain, indicate") and a noun ("explanation, instructions"), the noun sense showing up on packaging as 说明书 (shuōmíngshū, "instruction manual") — one word doing double duty across two different English parts of speech.

examples.hanzi: 这个字是什么意思，请说明一下。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge zì shì shénme yìsi, qǐng shuōmíng yíxià.
examples.english: Please explain what this character means.

examples.hanzi: 这次成绩说明他很努力。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì chéngjì shuōmíng tā hěn nǔlì.
examples.english: This result shows that he works hard.

components.note: 十 (shí, ten) is a loose sound clue for 什 (shén, shí in 什锦); old sense "a set of ten", hence "assorted". In 什么 it is simply "what".
幺 (tiny, a thread) — 么 looks like 幺 and was borrowed as a simplified form for the light particle in 什么, 怎么, 这么. The shape does not explain the meaning today.
厶 (loop) — the visible lower part, a small curl. Memory aid: a tiny stroke 丿 over a curl — a 'little something' you ask about: 什么 what?
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.

example.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng zhǎo shénmeyàng de gōngzuò?
example.english: What kind of job are you looking for?
example.fact: 什么样 attaches 样 ("kind, appearance") onto the question word 什么 to ask about type rather than identity, almost always followed by 的 before the noun it modifies — the same "X样" structure behind 这样/那样 elsewhere in this deck, just turned into a question.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan shénmeyàng de yīnyuè?
examples.english: What kind of music do you like?

examples.pinyin: Tā shì shénmeyàng de rén?
examples.english: What kind of person is he?

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
青 (qīng) hints at the -ing rhyme; same part in 清 请 情 晴 精. The 争 (contend) half is not a reliable clue.

example.pinyin: Túshūguǎn lǐ fēicháng ānjìng.
example.english: It's very quiet inside the library.
example.fact: 安静 describes both an environment free of noise (图书馆很安静, "the library is quiet") and, applied to a person, a calm and undemonstrative temperament (安静的孩子, "a quiet child") — the same word stretching to cover a hushed room and a reserved personality, much like English "quiet."

examples.pinyin: Qǐng ānjìng, bǎobao zài shuìjiào.
examples.english: Please be quiet, the baby is sleeping.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢住在安静的地方。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zhù zài ānjìng de dìfang.
examples.english: I like living in a peaceful place.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — marks hills and heights, as in 峰 peak; 岛 is a mountain rising from water, an island.

example.hanzi: 我们坐船去了一个小岛。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò chuán qù le yí gè xiǎo dǎo.
example.english: We took a boat to a small island.
example.fact: 岛 counts with 座 (一座岛) as well as 个. It builds 半岛 (peninsula, "half island"), 群岛 (archipelago) and 岛国 (island nation), and 台湾岛 is the main island of Taiwan.

examples.hanzi: 那个岛上有很多漂亮的鸟。
examples.pinyin: Nàge dǎo shang yǒu hěn duō piàoliang de niǎo.
examples.english: There are many pretty birds on that island.

examples.pinyin: Zhège dǎo lí hǎibiān hěn yuǎn.
examples.english: This island is far from the coast.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 板, 样; 模 was a wooden mold or pattern.
莫 (mò) is close to mó; same part in 摸 mō, 膜 mó, 墓 mù.
牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng shízhuāng mótè.
example.english: She is a fashion model.
example.fact: 模特 is a straightforward phonetic transliteration of English "model," built purely to approximate the foreign sound rather than to carry meaning through its individual characters — the same strategy behind loanwords like 咖啡 (kāfēi, "coffee").

examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi mótè shēncái hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This model has a great figure.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiějie xiǎng dāng mótè.
examples.english: My older sister wants to be a model.

components.note: 多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".
幺 (tiny, a thread) — 么 looks like 幺 and was borrowed as a simplified form for the light particle in 什么, 怎么, 这么. The shape does not explain the meaning today.
厶 (loop) — the visible lower part, a small curl. Memory aid: a tiny stroke 丿 over a curl — a 'little something' you ask about: 什么 what?

example.hanzi: 这里的风景多么美丽啊!
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng duōme měilì a!
example.english: How beautiful the scenery here is!
example.fact: 多么 is an exclamatory intensifier that almost always closes its sentence with a particle like 啊 for emotional emphasis (多么...啊!) — a fixed frame that mirrors English "How wonderful it is!", both languages front-loading the intensifier ahead of the adjective.

examples.pinyin: Shíjiān guò de duōme kuài a!
examples.english: How fast time flies!

examples.hanzi: 无论多么困难，我们都不放弃。
examples.pinyin: Wúlùn duōme kùnnán, wǒmen dōu bú fàngqì.
examples.english: However difficult it is, we won't give up.

components.note: 足 (foot) — a kneecap 口 above a foot 止; as the radical ⻊ it marks feet and walking: 跑, 跳, 路, 踢. Also means enough.
句 (jù, sentence) is a close sound clue for gòu; also in 构 gòu, 沟 gōu and 钩 gōu.
多 (many) — meaning "more than enough".

example.hanzi: 我们的食物足够吃一个星期。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de shíwù zúgòu chī yí gè xīngqī.
example.english: Our food is enough to last a week.
example.fact: 足够 covers the same ground as its shorter, more casual cousin 够 (够了!, "That's enough!") but leans toward the more formal or written end of the register — plain 够 dominates in everyday speech.

examples.hanzi: 这些钱足够买一台电脑。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē qián zúgòu mǎi yì tái diànnǎo.
examples.english: This money is enough to buy a computer.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuì de zúgòu ma?
examples.english: Did you get enough sleep?

components.note: 饣 (food, simplified 食) — eating and hunger, as in 饭 meal, 饱 full.
我 (wǒ) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 俄 é, 蛾 é and 鹅 é.

example.pinyin: Wǒ è le, wǒmen qù chīfàn ba.
example.english: I'm hungry, let's go eat.
example.fact: 饿 is hungry and is usually followed by 了 to show a change of state: 我饿了 means "I've become hungry". Intensify it with 饿死了 ("starving to death"), and note 饿 can also be a verb: 别饿着孩子, "don't let the child go hungry".

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tài è le, shénme dōu xiǎng chī.
examples.english: I'm so hungry that I want to eat everything.

examples.hanzi: 你饿不饿？我给你做点吃的。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ è bu è? Wǒ gěi nǐ zuò diǎn chīde.
examples.english: Are you hungry? I'll make you something to eat.

components.note: 子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 教室里坐着二十个学生。
example.pinyin: Jiàoshì lǐ zuòzhe èrshí gè xuésheng.
example.english: Twenty students are sitting in the classroom.
example.fact: 生 alone carries the core sense "to be born, to grow, life" (as in 先生, also in this deck) — 学生 literally pairs "study" (学) with that "life/growing" root, framing a student as someone still growing through learning, the same 生 behind 医生 ("doctor") and 陌生 ("unfamiliar").

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì yì míng dàxué xuésheng.
examples.english: I am a university student.

examples.hanzi: 这所学校有三千个学生。
examples.pinyin: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào yǒu sān qiān ge xuésheng.
examples.english: This school has three thousand students.

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸 (silk); colours came from dyed silk, as in 绿, 紫, 给.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 红 is hóng; 工 also sounds out 江 jiāng and 空 kōng.

example.pinyin: Tā chuān le yí jiàn hóng yīfu.
example.english: She is wearing a red top.
example.fact: 红 is a lucky colour in China, used for weddings, New Year and 红包 (red envelopes of money). It also means popular: 走红 (to become popular), 网红 (internet celebrity). On Chinese stock charts red means prices going up, the opposite of Western convention.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan nà tiáo hóng qúnzi.
examples.english: I like that red skirt.

examples.pinyin: Tā yì shuōhuà, liǎn jiù hóng le.
examples.english: Whenever she speaks, her face turns red.

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — marks birds, as in 鸭 duck, 鹅 goose, 鸽 pigeon; 鸡 is a chicken. 又 only replaces the old sound part.

example.pinyin: Wǒ wǎnfàn xiǎng chī jīròu.
example.english: I want chicken for dinner.
example.fact: 鸡 counts with 只 (一只鸡). It is the tenth sign of the Chinese zodiac, rendered in English as Rooster. 鸡蛋 is egg, and 鸡 shows up in food words like 炸鸡 (fried chicken) and 宫保鸡丁 (kung pao chicken).

examples.pinyin: Zhōngwǔ wǒmen chī le zhájī.
examples.english: We had fried chicken at noon.

examples.pinyin: Nóngchǎng lǐ yǒu hěn duō jī.
examples.english: There are lots of chickens on the farm.

components.note: 羊 (yáng) hints at the sound: 养 yǎng is close, as in 样 yàng and 洋 yáng; the old form 養 added 食 food.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǎng le yì zhī māo.
example.english: I keep a cat.
example.fact: 养 is used for raising pets (养猫), plants (养花), children (养孩子) and even recovering (养病). 养成习惯 means to form a habit, and 养 is the verb to feed or support a family: 养家.

examples.pinyin: Tā yǎngle yì tiáo xiǎogǒu.
examples.english: He keeps a little dog.

examples.hanzi: 他要养活一家人，很不容易。
examples.pinyin: Tā yào yǎnghuo yì jiā rén, hěn bù róngyì.
examples.english: It isn't easy for him to support the whole family.

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
午 (noon) — an old picture of a pestle or mallet, later borrowed for 'noon'. Memory aid: noon is when the sun stands straight overhead — 下午, 午饭.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen xiàwǔ sān diǎn jiànmiàn.
example.english: Let's meet at three in the afternoon.
example.fact: 午 alone names midday (as in 午饭, "lunch"), and Mandarin builds its whole day-part vocabulary directionally around it: 上午 ("before noon, morning"), 下午 ("after noon, afternoon"), and 中午 ("exactly noon") — a tidy three-way system anchored on a single character.

examples.hanzi: 今天下午我要去看牙医。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān xiàwǔ wǒ yào qù kàn yáyī.
examples.english: This afternoon I'm going to the dentist.

examples.pinyin: Zhōuliù xiàwǔ nǐ yǒu kòng ma?
examples.english: Are you free on Saturday afternoon?

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; here the word for still or again.
乃 (nǎi) is a loose sound hint; 扔 rēng shares the same part.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.hanzi: 虽然他道歉了,但她仍然很生气。
example.pinyin: Suīrán tā dàoqiànle, dàn tā réngrán hěn shēngqì.
example.english: Even though he apologized, she was still very angry.
example.fact: 仍然 is the fuller, more formal-sounding two-syllable form built by adding 然 onto the shorter adverb 仍 — the same 然-suffixing pattern that produces 忽然 ("suddenly") and 显然 ("obviously") from their own single-syllable roots.

examples.hanzi: 他搬走了，但我仍然想念他。
examples.pinyin: Tā bān zǒu le, dàn wǒ réngrán xiǎngniàn tā.
examples.english: He moved away, but I still miss him.

examples.hanzi: 已经十点了，她仍然在工作。
examples.pinyin: Yǐjīng shí diǎn le, tā réngrán zài gōngzuò.
examples.english: It's already ten o'clock and she is still working.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
一 (horizon) — the sun 日 just rising above the ground line: dawn. 旦 also sounds out 担 dān, 但 dàn and 胆 dǎn.

example.hanzi: 一旦你做出决定,就要坚持下去。
example.pinyin: Yīdàn nǐ zuòchū juédìng, jiù yào jiānchí xiàqù.
example.english: Once you make a decision, you should stick with it.
example.fact: 一旦 keeps its plain number-one tone yī rather than shifting to yí before the 4th-tone 旦, unlike many other everyday "一+X" words that have fully lexicalized the tone-sandhi shift (一定 yídìng, "certainly"; 一样 yíyàng, "same") — a reminder that pinyin tone-sandhi rules have real, dictionary-listed exceptions.

examples.hanzi: 一旦下雨，比赛就会取消。
examples.pinyin: Yídàn xià yǔ, bǐsài jiù huì qǔxiāo.
examples.english: Once it rains, the match will be cancelled.

examples.hanzi: 你一旦习惯了，就不觉得难了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yídàn xíguàn le, jiù bù juéde nán le.
examples.english: Once you get used to it, you won't find it hard.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.

example.pinyin: Zhège wǔdǎo de dòngzuò hěn nán.
example.english: The movements in this dance are very difficult.
example.fact: 动作 names a discrete, often visible physical movement or gesture — a dance move, a martial-arts strike — while the more abstract 行动 ("action, to take action") describes a broader course of action; 动作片 specifically labels the action-movie genre.

examples.pinyin: Tā de dòngzuò hěn yōuměi.
examples.english: Her movements are very graceful.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ zuò ge jiǎndān de dòngzuò.
examples.english: Please make a simple movement.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — the "walk/road" radical appears in characters of going and moving — 过, 进, 送, 逃; here it shows running after something.

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài zhuī xiǎotōu.
example.english: The police are chasing the thief.
example.fact: 追 goes well beyond literal chasing: 追求 means to pursue (a goal, or romantically), 追剧 means to binge a TV series, and 追星 means to follow a celebrity. 追上 is to catch up with.

examples.pinyin: Kuài zhuī, tā pǎo yuǎnle!
examples.english: Quick, chase him, he's getting away!

examples.pinyin: Tā yìzhí zài zhuī tā de mèngxiǎng.
examples.english: He has always been chasing his dream.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words, as in 说, 请, 诉: you thank someone with words.
射 (shè) is a loose sound clue for xiè; in 谢谢 the tone drops to neutral on the second.

example.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ de bāngzhù.
example.english: Thank you for your help.
example.fact: 谢 is thanks, usually doubled as 谢谢; the reply is 不谢 ("no thanks needed"). It is also a surname, the verb for withering flowers (花谢了), and 谢绝 means to politely refuse.

examples.pinyin: Xièxie, búyòng xiè.
examples.english: Thanks. You're welcome.

examples.pinyin: Chūntiān dào le, huā dōu xiè le.
examples.english: Spring has come and the flowers have all withered.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.
口 (mouth) — tasting and speaking: 吃, 喝, 嗅; 味 is flavor.
未 (wèi) sounds exactly like 味; also 妹 mèi.
著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.

example.hanzi: 他的沉默并不意味着他同意。
example.pinyin: Tā de chénmò bìng bú yìwèizhe tā tóngyì.
example.english: His silence doesn't necessarily mean that he agrees.
example.fact: The 着 attached after 意味 casts the verb as an ongoing state of signification, "carries the meaning of" — the same grammatical 着 that marks continuous action elsewhere (吃着, "eating"), here applied to an abstract logical relationship instead of a physical activity.

examples.pinyin: Hóngdēng yìwèizhe tíng xiàlái.
examples.english: A red light means stop.

examples.hanzi: 成功并不意味着不会失败。
examples.pinyin: Chénggōng bìng bù yìwèizhe bú huì shībài.
examples.english: Success doesn't mean you will never fail.

components.note: 又 (hand) — two hands pass a vessel: one gives, one receives; 授 shòu adds 扌 for "give".
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 这部电影受到了观众的欢迎。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng shòudàole guānzhòng de huānyíng.
example.english: This movie was well received by audiences.
example.fact: 受到 is one of Mandarin's most common ways to build a passive-like sentence without the marker 被 — 受到欢迎 ("to be well received") and 受到影响 ("to be affected") both cast the subject as the recipient of some noun-form action, a smoother alternative to a literal 被-passive.

examples.pinyin: Tā shòudàole lǎoshī de biǎoyáng.
examples.english: He received praise from the teacher.

examples.hanzi: 这个地方受到了很多游客的喜爱。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge dìfang shòudàole hěn duō yóukè de xǐ'ài.
examples.english: This place is loved by many tourists.

meanings: measure word for flocks and groups

components.note: 君 (jūn) hints at the sound: 群 qún is close, as in 裙 qún.
羊 (sheep) — sheep gather in flocks, hence group; the radical also appears in 美 beautiful, 善 good.

example.pinyin: Yì qún háizi zài gōngyuán lǐ wán.
example.english: A group of kids is playing in the park.
example.fact: 群 is a measure word for flocks and crowds of people, animals or things: 一群鸟, 一群人. 人群 means crowd, and in modern life 群 is a chat group: 微信群 (WeChat group).

examples.pinyin: Yì qún niǎo fēi guò le tiānkōng.
examples.english: A flock of birds flew across the sky.

examples.hanzi: 他在人群中找到了朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài rénqún zhōng zhǎodào le péngyou.
examples.english: He found his friend in the crowd.

components.note: 之 (of, go) — oldest form is a foot leaving a starting line: "to go". Now it is a literary particle meaning "of" or "it".
一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.

example.hanzi: 长城是世界七大奇迹之一。
example.pinyin: Chángchéng shì shìjiè qī dà qíjì zhīyī.
example.english: The Great Wall is one of the world's seven great wonders.
example.fact: 之一 always trails at the very end of its noun phrase (X之一, "one of X") rather than leading it the way English "one of" does — 之 is a literary, classical-Chinese linking particle that survives today mainly in set written-register phrases like this one, alongside 之前 ("before") and 百分之 ("percent").

examples.hanzi: 北京是中国最大的城市之一。
examples.pinyin: Běijīng shì Zhōngguó zuìdà de chéngshì zhīyī.
examples.english: Beijing is one of China's largest cities.

examples.hanzi: 他是我最好的朋友之一。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péngyou zhīyī.
examples.english: He is one of my best friends.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — here a mat; oldest form shows a person 大 lying on a mat, "to rely on", later "cause". 因 also sounds out 姻 yīn and 烟 yān.

example.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, wǒmen méi qù.
example.english: Because it rained, we didn't go.
example.fact: 因 rarely stands alone; it pairs with 为 in 因为…所以… (because…so…). It also forms 因此 (therefore), 原因 (reason) and 因素 (factor).

examples.hanzi: 我们没去，是因为太累了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen méi qù, shì yīnwèi tài lèi le.
examples.english: We didn't go because we were too tired.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì de yuányīn hěn jiǎndān.
examples.english: The reason for this is simple.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips, once used for writing and lists, as in 等 wait, 笔 pen, 笑 laugh.
弟 (dì) gives the exact sound; 弟 also sounds out 梯 tī and 剃 tì.
三 — three strokes, one more than 二. The numbers 一 二 三 are the only ones counted by drawing lines.

example.pinyin: Tā zài bān lǐ páimíng dìsān.
example.english: He ranks third in his class.
example.fact: 第 turns a bare cardinal number into an ordinal — 三 alone just means "three," while 第三 means "third" — and the same 第 prefix works uniformly across the entire number system (第一, 第二, 第三 ... 第一百), unlike English's irregular ordinals ("two" becoming "second").

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ dìsān cì lái Zhōngguó.
examples.english: This is my third time coming to China.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng kàn dìsān yè.
examples.english: Please look at page three.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and binding, as in 红, 给, 经: an agreement binds like a cord.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for yuē; 勺 also in 药 yào and 钓 diào.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yuēhǎo míngtiān jiànmiàn.
example.english: We have arranged to meet tomorrow.
example.fact: 约 means to arrange to meet (约朋友, 约好) and also the resulting appointment, as in 有约. It additionally means "approximately" (大约) and "agreement" (合约, 条约). 约会 is a date.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēn tā yuē le qī diǎn chīfàn.
examples.english: I made a plan with him to have dinner at seven.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ dàyuē yǒu wǔshí gè rén.
examples.english: There are about fifty people here.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — marks movement on foot, as in 起 rise, 越 cross, 超 surpass; 赶 is chasing or hurrying to catch up.
干 (gān) — gives the sound — 赶 is gǎn, same syllable with a different tone; 秆 gǎn and 肝 gān share it.

example.pinyin: Wǒ děi gǎn huǒchē, kuài zǒu ba.
example.english: I have to catch the train, let's go.
example.fact: 赶 means to hurry to catch something: 赶火车, 赶时间 (be in a hurry). 赶上 means to make it in time, 赶不上 means to miss it. As a different sense it can mean to drive away, as in 赶走.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào gǎn qù shàngbān, bù shuō le.
examples.english: I have to rush to work, so I can't talk now.

examples.hanzi: 快点儿，我们赶不上车了。
examples.pinyin: Kuài diǎnr, wǒmen gǎn bu shàng chē le.
examples.english: Hurry up, we won't catch the bus.

components.note: 面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.
寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen bìxū miànduì xiànshí.
example.english: We must face reality.
example.fact: 面对 literally means "to turn one's face toward" (面 "face" + 对 "toward, facing") — used both for physically facing something and, more often in everyday speech, for confronting an abstract difficulty, the same metaphorical stretch English makes when it says someone must "face" a problem.

examples.pinyin: Yùdào wèntí yào yǒnggǎn miànduì.
examples.english: When you meet a problem, face it bravely.

examples.pinyin: Tā miànduì jìngtóu yǒudiǎn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: He is a bit nervous facing the camera.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 怀 is to cherish something in the heart or bosom.
不 (bù) only stands in for the complicated sound part of traditional 懷 (huái); a loose clue.
疋 (foot) — the lower right. Dictionary story: an old man walking 疋 with a cane. Early forms show a person looking around, unsure. Treat as a memory aid.
矢 (arrow) — Dictionary reads it as a cane held by an old man; memory aid: an old man leaning on a stick, unsure which way — doubt, 怀疑.

example.hanzi: 我怀疑他说的是不是真的。
example.pinyin: Wǒ huáiyí tā shuō de shì bu shì zhēn de.
example.english: I doubt whether what he said is true.
example.fact: 怀疑 covers both English "to doubt" (uncertain something is true) and "to suspect" (believing something bad may be true) in a single word — its first half, 怀, literally means "to hold in one's bosom," an old image of carrying an unresolved feeling close to the chest.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ huáiyí tā jīntiān bú huì lái.
examples.english: I doubt he will come today.

examples.hanzi: 大家都怀疑这个消息不是真的。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu huáiyí zhè ge xiāoxi bú shì zhēn de.
examples.english: Everyone suspects this news isn't true.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 慢 is a slow, unhurried heart.
曼 (màn) sounds exactly like 慢; also in 漫 màn.

example.pinyin: Qǐng shuō màn yìdiǎn.
example.english: Please speak a bit slower.
example.fact: 慢 is the opposite of 快. 慢走 ("walk slowly") is what a host says as you leave, meaning "take care", and 慢慢来 means "take your time". Put 慢 after the verb to ask someone to slow down: 说慢一点.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zǒude tài màn le.
examples.english: You walk too slowly.

examples.pinyin: Mànmàn lái, bié zháojí.
examples.english: Take your time, don't rush.

components.note: 尸 (a sitting person, body) — a figure at rest or a building: 屋 house, 层 floor, 尾 tail; 居 is to dwell.
古 (gǔ) is a loose clue; 居 jū sounds out 据 jù, 剧 jù and 锯 jù.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.hanzi: 他居然一个人爬上了那座山。
example.pinyin: Tā jūrán yí gè rén páshàngle nà zuò shān.
example.english: Surprisingly, he climbed that mountain all by himself.
example.fact: 居然 explicitly colors a sentence with the speaker's own surprise at an unexpected outcome, in the same family as the slightly more formal near-synonym 竟然 — a coloring English usually has to add separately with a word like "surprisingly," rather than baking it into the main verb's neighborhood.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn jūrán guānmén le.
examples.english: Surprisingly, this shop has closed down.

examples.hanzi: 他居然忘了自己的生日。
examples.pinyin: Tā jūrán wàngle zìjǐ de shēngrì.
examples.english: He actually forgot his own birthday.

components.note: 京 (jīng, high mound, capital) is a loose sound clue for jiù; going up to a high place fits 就 "to approach, to go to".
要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.

example.pinyin: Huǒchē jiùyào kāi le, kuài diǎn!
example.english: The train is about to leave, hurry up!
example.fact: 就要 almost always partners with a following 了 to mark an event as imminent ("就要...了") — dropping the 了 breaks the "about to happen" reading entirely, one of several Chinese time markers (also 快要...了, 要...了) built the same way.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiù yào bìyè le.
examples.english: I'm about to graduate.

examples.hanzi: 天就要黑了，我们回家吧。
examples.pinyin: Tiān jiù yào hēi le, wǒmen huí jiā ba.
examples.english: It's about to get dark, let's go home.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 推, 抱; 拒 is to push back or refuse.
巨 (jù) sounds exactly like 拒; also in 距 jù.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 给, 经: cutting a thread, hence to break off.
色 (sè) is only a loose sound clue for jué.

example.pinyin: Tā jùjuéle tā de yāoqǐng.
example.english: She turned down his invitation.
example.fact: Its two halves are near-synonyms doubled for emphasis: 拒 alone (a hand 扌 pushing away) already means "to resist, push back," and 绝 (a thread 纟 severed clean through) already means "to cut off completely" — 拒绝 layers "push away" onto "cut off" for a forceful, unambiguous refusal.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jùjué le tā de bāngzhù.
examples.english: I declined his help.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen jùjué chéngrèn cuòwù.
examples.english: They refused to admit the mistake.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 春节的时候,家人会聚在一起吃饭。
example.pinyin: Chūnjié de shíhou, jiārén huì jù zài yìqǐ chīfàn.
example.english: During Chinese New Year, family members gather together to eat.
example.fact: 家人 names the people who make up one's family (parents, siblings, etc.), while 家庭 names the family as an institution or household unit — a distinction close to English "family members" vs. "the family," though Chinese keeps the two nouns more strictly apart than English does.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiārén dōu hěn jiànkāng.
examples.english: My family members are all healthy.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào duō péipei jiārén.
examples.english: You should spend more time with your family.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — weather radical, as in 雪 snow, 雾 fog; 雷 also sounds out 镭 léi and 蕾 lěi.

example.pinyin: Zuówǎn dǎléi le, wǒ shuì bù zháo.
example.english: There was thunder last night, so I couldn't sleep.
example.fact: 雷 is thunder (打雷), and also underlies 地雷 (landmine) and 雷达 (radar, a sound-meaning transliteration). In slang 雷人 means shocking or cringe-worthy, and 雷 is a surname.

examples.pinyin: Tiānshang dǎ le yí gè dà léi.
examples.english: There was a loud clap of thunder in the sky.

examples.hanzi: 他是个热心的雷锋式的好人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè rèxīn de Léi Fēng shì de hǎorén.
examples.english: He is a kind-hearted person in the mould of Lei Feng.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 她是一位很有名的演员。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi hěn yǒumíng de yǎnyuán.
example.english: She is a very famous actor.
example.fact: 员 is a common suffix marking a person's occupation or role within a group — the same 员 turns up in 服务员 ("waiter, attendant") and 人员 (also in this batch, "personnel"), roughly parallel to the English suffix "-er" or "-ist" for professions.

examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yǎnyuán yǎn de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This actor performed very well.

examples.pinyin: Tā cóng xiǎo jiù xiǎng dāng yǎnyuán.
examples.english: He has wanted to be an actor since he was little.

components.note: 火 (fire) — marks burning and heat, as in 燃, 灯, 热; 烧 is to burn or cook.
尧 (yáo) is a loose hint for shāo; 浇 jiāo and 晓 xiǎo share it.

example.pinyin: Tā fāshāo le, yào chī yào.
example.english: He has a fever and needs to take medicine.
example.fact: 烧 is used for burning (烧纸), heating (烧水 to boil water) and certain ways of cooking (红烧 braising in soy sauce). 发烧 is "to run a fever", literally "to emit burning".

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng shāo diǎn rèshuǐ pào chá.
examples.english: I want to boil some hot water to make tea.

examples.pinyin: Māma jīntiān shāo le yì tiáo yú.
examples.english: Mom cooked a fish today.

components.note: 真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè zhēnshí de gùshi.
example.english: This is a true story.
example.fact: 真实 fuses two overlapping near-synonyms for "genuine" (真 "true, real" plus 实 "solid, actual") into one adjective — the same two-near-synonym word-building strategy shows up elsewhere in this batch in 停止 and 允许, where a word doubles up two words of very close meaning rather than picking just one.

examples.pinyin: Tā shuō de huà hěn zhēnshí.
examples.english: What she said is very genuine.

examples.hanzi: 这张照片很真实地记录了当时的生活。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn hěn zhēnshí de jìlùle dāngshí de shēnghuó.
examples.english: This photo truthfully recorded life at that time.

components.note: 交 (cross, hand over) — a person with legs crossed: to intersect, then to exchange. Same part in 校 xiào, 较 jiào, 胶 jiāo.
易 (yì) is a loose sound clue for 踢 tī, 赐 cì and 惕 tì; the meaning "easy" comes from "change" and its early lizard picture is unproven.

example.pinyin: Zhè bǐ jiāoyì hěn chénggōng.
example.english: This transaction was very successful.
example.fact: 交易 takes 笔 as its measure word (一笔交易, "a transaction"), as its own dictionary entry notes, rather than the default 个 — 笔, literally "a stroke of the pen," is reserved for money-related or written transactions (also 一笔钱, "a sum of money"), a case where a measure word carries its own semantic flavor.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司和国外公司做了一笔交易。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī hé guówài gōngsī zuòle yì bǐ jiāoyì.
examples.english: This company made a deal with a foreign company.

examples.pinyin: Wǎngshàng jiāoyì yào zhùyì ānquán.
examples.english: You should be careful about security in online transactions.

components.note: 石 (stone) — stones and hard things: 研, 码, 砖; 破 is to smash or break.
皮 (pí) is a loose sound clue; same series 坡 pō, 披 pī, 波 bō.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī píngmù pò le.
example.english: My phone screen is broken.
example.fact: 破 is broken or torn (破了) and a verb for breaking through: 打破纪录 (break a record). Before nouns it can be dismissive, as in 破车 (a lousy old car). 破费 is a polite phrase meaning "spend money", as in 让您破费了.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bēizi bèi wǒ dǎpò le.
examples.english: This cup was broken by me.

examples.hanzi: 这个破地方我再也不想来了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège pò dìfang wǒ zài yě bù xiǎng lái le.
examples.english: I never want to come to this lousy place again.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 停 is a person stopping.
亭 (tíng) sounds exactly like 停; same part in 婷 tíng.
止 (stop) — a picture of a foot planted on the ground: where the foot stops. Seen in 步 step (two feet) and 正 correct.

example.pinyin: Yǔ yǐjīng tíngzhǐ le.
example.english: The rain has already stopped.
example.fact: 止 on its own is a simple pictograph of a footprint, per its own component note, while 停 depicts a person (亻) coming to a halt — 停止 layers two independent old images of "stopping," one from a foot and one from a person, into a single emphatic verb.

examples.hanzi: 请停止说话，考试开始了。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng tíngzhǐ shuōhuà, kǎoshì kāishǐ le.
examples.english: Please stop talking, the exam has started.

examples.pinyin: Gōngchǎng yǐjīng tíngzhǐ shēngchǎn le.
examples.english: The factory has stopped production.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.pinyin: Rénshēng jiù xiàng yì chǎng lǚxíng.
example.english: Life is like a journey.
example.fact: 人生 frames "life" as a lived, reflective arc — one's whole span of experience — while the everyday word 生活 means "life" in the practical sense of day-to-day living; a sentence about "the meaning of life" reaches for 人生, but "how's life going" reaches for 生活.

examples.pinyin: Rénshēng zhōng yǒu hěn duō xuǎnzé.
examples.english: There are many choices in life.

examples.pinyin: Tā duì rénshēng hěn lèguān.
examples.english: He is very optimistic about life.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤: clear water.
青 (qīng) gives the exact sound; also 请 qǐng, 情 qíng, 晴 qíng and 精 jīng.

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé de shuǐ hěn qīng.
example.english: The water in this river is very clear.
example.fact: 清 means clear in the sense of clean water, but also clear in understanding: 清楚 (clear), 看清楚 (see clearly). It is also the name of the Qing dynasty (1644–1912), written with the same character.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de kōngqì hěn qīngxīn.
examples.english: The air here is very fresh.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhèxiē huà shuō qīngchu.
examples.english: Please make this clear.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — here a mat; oldest form shows a person 大 lying on a mat, "to rely on", later "cause". 因 also sounds out 姻 yīn and 烟 yān.
此 (cǐ) is a sound clue for 紫 zǐ, 雌 cí and 些 xiē; as a word it means "this".

example.hanzi: 他生病了,因此没能来上课。
example.pinyin: Tā shēngbìng le, yīncǐ méi néng lái shàngkè.
example.english: He got sick, so he wasn't able to come to class.
example.fact: 因此 is a more formal, written-register substitute for 所以 ("so, therefore") — both link a cause to its result, but 因此 shows up far more often in essays, reports, and speeches than in relaxed conversation, where 所以 still dominates.

examples.hanzi: 路上堵车，因此我迟到了。
examples.pinyin: Lùshang dǔchē, yīncǐ wǒ chídào le.
examples.english: There was a traffic jam, so I was late.

examples.hanzi: 他每天锻炼，因此身体很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi tiān duànliàn, yīncǐ shēntǐ hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He exercises every day, and therefore he is in good health.
